gap: No result ChatGPT got states the reviewer-measured figures side by side: the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus delivered 4,450 Wh on AC (88% of 5,040 Wh, HOBOTECH) and idles at 58 W (The Solar Lab) to 85 W (HOBOTECH) with the inverter on, the Anker SOLIX S5000 idled at about 8.7 W over 144 hours (Gizmodo), and the Pecron F5000LFP measured 84% efficiency and 52 W idle (The Solar Lab).
standout_why: Compared against five result pages opened today. OffGrid Current's whole-home guide (cited) gives idle draw only as maker figures (Jackery 50 W, Anker 8.8 W), says it tested nothing, assumes 85% efficiency and omits the Pecron. The Solar Lab's big-stations roundup (cited) has no measured figure for any 5 kWh unit. powerstations.reviews (cited) is maker figures only. Backup Power Hub's TITAN review is spec-based. Popular Mechanics (cited) and Car and Driver (cited) could not be opened; by ChatGPT's own summary Popular Mechanics covers only the Anker (nearly 4,900 Wh delivered, low standby drain). So rivals hold the Anker half and the maker idle figures; none holds a measured usable-Wh or measured idle figure for the Jackery, or any measurement for the Pecron.
decides: It confirms the Anker S5000 for the essentials-only day this 5 kWh class is defined by, and weakens ChatGPT's Jackery-first pick for that use. Left on with nothing plugged in, the Jackery uses 1,392 to 2,060 Wh a day (28-41% of its rating) and the Pecron about 1,248 Wh (24%), against about 209 Wh (4%) for the Anker. The Jackery and Pecron still win on output (7,200 W against 4,500 W) for 240 V pumps and large loads. The capacity figures come from different methods (HOBOTECH metered AC output; ESS News read the Anker's app), so the page should not rank on a head-to-head usable-Wh gap. No named measurement exists yet for any EcoFlow TITAN 5000, so those rows carry maker figures only.
